title: Order-invariance — 11 machine-checked theorems of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit and how they are bound
description:
Order-invariance — 11 machine-checked theorems of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit, one Lean namespace, wing the floor. 11 close by exhaustion over a finite domain (by decide); 1 rfl declaration(s) are listed and not sealed, by design. Every one is sealed live in the append-only ledger.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used in this deposit's honest sense: correlation by derivation, not quantum entanglement, and no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 5 definition(s) are used by two or more theorems, binding 32 pair(s); the theorems fall into 2 strand(s), the largest of 8. Most binding: perms (7), receipt (4), ghzXSupport (3), naive (2), par3 (2).

2 · Imports. Built on: no other cluster. Built on it: no other cluster. Checking this cluster needs 1 file(s): src/proof/quantum.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 11 sealed receipts fold to 18d30f2b-d336-8caf-9a47-146ae047dfc4. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed on this run. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (8, 1, 0, 3, 3, 7, 7). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs observed among each theorem's seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: rights.lean (3 observed, 0.98 expected, lift 3.07), elementary.lean (8 observed, 3.9 expected, lift 2.05), recovered.lean (3 observed, 1.83 expected, lift 1.64). A lift near 1 is what chance gives. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 16.18; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.51. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). Chance, measured: over 200 reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to (seeded, so every rebuild gives the same numbers), a best lift at least this high arose in 61.0% of them — consistent with chance.

Prior art. sorting a multiset into a canonical order BEFORE folding it is standard practice, not a discovery here. Sorted-leaf Merkle trees are the recommended construction for multiproofs and are shipped that way in OpenZeppelin's merkle-tree library; canonical ordering before hashing is long-established in cryptographic serialisation generally. The mathematical content is elementary: any function of a canonical form is invariant under permutation of its input, which is why `receipt_is_order_invariant` holds. What this file contributes is the Lean verification over a stated finite domain and the negative controls beside it — `naive_fold_is_not_order_invariant` shows the property is bought by the sort and not free, and `the_receipt_is_not_injective` and `the_invariance_is_canonicalisation_not_physics` state its limits. Verification and refusal, not discovery. Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json. No novelty is claimed here.

The theorems.

  1. perms_of_four_is_factorial — (perms [1, 2, 4, 8]).length = 24 record
  2. receipt_is_order_invariant — (perms [1, 2, 4, 8]).all (fun p => receipt p == receipt [1, 2, 4, 8]) record
  3. receipt_order_invariant_on_the_orbit — (perms [1, 2, 4, 8, 7, 5]).all (fun p => receipt p == receipt [1, 2, 4, 8, 7, 5]) record
  4. naive_fold_is_not_order_invariant — ¬ ((perms [1, 2, 4, 8]).all (fun p => naive p == naive [1, 2, 4, 8])) record
  5. superposition_collapses_to_one — ((perms [1, 2, 4, 8]).map receipt).eraseDups.length = 1 record
  6. the_invariance_is_canonicalisation_not_physics — (perms [1, 2, 4, 8]).all (fun p => sort p == sort [1, 2, 4, 8]) record
  7. the_receipt_is_not_injective — pairsOverNine.length = 45 ∧ (pairsOverNine.map receipt).eraseDups.length = 9 record
  8. the_uncanonicalised_fold_gives_many_answers — ((perms [1, 2, 4, 8]).map naive).eraseDups.length = 5 record
  9. the_ghz_x_support_is_exactly_the_even_parity_strings — (List.range 8).filter (fun n => par3 n == 0) = ghzXSupport record
  10. it_is_half_of_the_eight — ghzXSupport.length = 4 ∧ (List.range 8).length = 8 record
  11. a_classical_mixture_reaches_the_parity_ghz_never_does — ((List.range 8).filter (fun n => par3 n == 1)).length = 4 ∧ ((List.range 8).filter (fun n => par3 n == 1)).all (fun n => ¬ ghzXSupport.contains n) record
